title: Anthropic halka arz için resmi başvuruyu SEC'ye sundu
summary: Yapay zeka girişimi Anthropic, Nasdaq borsasında ANT koduyla işlem görmek üzere ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu'na S-1 kayıt formunu iletti.
body:
Yapay zeka şirketi Anthropic, PBC, ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu'na (SEC) Form S-1 kayıt beyanını ileterek halka arz sürecini başlattı. Şirket, A Grubu adi hisselerini **Nasdaq Global Select Market** üzerinde "ANT" sembolüyle işlem görmek üzere listelemeyi hedefliyor.

## Anthropic halka arz dosyasında öne çıkanlar

Resmi duyuruya göre halka arz edilecek A Grubu hisse adedi ve hisse başına fiyat aralığı henüz netleşmedi. Yatırımcılara sunulacak izahname taslağının Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC ve Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC üzerinden temin edilebileceği bildirildi. SEC'ye iletilen tescil beyanının henüz yürürlüğe girmediği ve hisse satışlarının bu tescil tamamlanmadan başlayamayacağı hatırlatıldı.

## Kamu yararına hisse taahhüdü genişletildi

Anthropic, halka arz başvurusunun yanı sıra **Anthropic Public Benefit Fund** adını verdiği yeni bir girişim kurduğunu da duyurdu. Hissedarların onayına tabi olarak şirketin yüzde 5'lik hissesi doğrudan bu fona tahsis edilecek. Şirketin değerlemesi belirli bir eşiğin üzerine her yüzde 50 arttığında, yönetim kurulu kararıyla fona yüzde 2'lik ek pay eklenebilecek.

Anthropic kurucularının kuruluş aşamasında hisselerinin yüzde 80'ini bağışlama taahhüdü ve çalışanlara yönelik hisse bağış eşleme programı da dikkate alındığında, şirketin yaklaşık yüzde 20'si kamu yararı projelerine ayrılmış olacak. Bir Limited Liability Company (LLC) olarak yapılandırılan fon, yapay zekanın iş gücü piyasasına etkileri ve kamu yararı taşıyan projelere doğrudan dağıtım yapabilecek ancak lobi veya siyasi bağış amaçlı fon sağlamayacak.

**Neden önemli?** Üretken yapay zeka alanında öncü modeller geliştiren Anthropic'in halka arz adımı, sektördeki finansman arayışını kamu piyasalarına taşırken şirketin kamusal fayda misyonunu hisse yapısına doğrudan bağlayan bir model sunuyor.

source_texts.text:
- Oct 21, 2026 Physicist Christopher Stubbs joins Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust Dr. Christopher Stubbs, an experimental physicist and former Dean of Science at Harvard University, has joined Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust. He brings to the Trust decades of scientific expertise across observational cosmology and precision measurement.
- Oct 2, 2026 Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap Anthropic is investing $100 million in Claude Frontier Academy to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by the end of 2027, with cohorts from Accenture, Bain, CBA, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk already underway.
- Aug 27, 2026 Expanding our support for scientists Starting today, 10,000 scientists around the world can get Claude at no cost to start. Verified principal investigators qualify for a Claude Team subscription plan and then add their research team to Standard seats for free, or Premium seats for $15 per month, for up to a year.
- Jul 20, 2026 Apply for Anthropic’s AI for Science rare disease research grants Anthropic is sharing a focused call for AI for Science applications centered specifically on rare genetic diseases. Accepted applicants will receive up to $50,000 in Claude credits over six months, with the goal of building a community of researchers looking into how AI can reshape our understanding of rare disease.

source_texts.title: Investing in the public benefit
source_texts.text:
Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.
As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.
The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.
One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.
We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as an LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.
Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.
This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.
In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.

source_texts.title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering
source_texts.text:
Today, Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission relating to its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.” The number of shares of Class A common stock to be offered and the price range for the proposed offering have not yet been determined.
The proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus, when available, may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014.
A registration statement relating to these securities has been filed with the SEC but has not yet become effective. These securities may not be sold, nor may offers to buy be accepted, prior to the time the registration statement becomes effective. Today’s announcement does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.
